chunks: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Ali ibn Shajarah, from his uncle Bashir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dark-skinned woman picking up manure or camel dung from the ground, so the Muslims said, 'The way, O Messenger of Allah!' The dark-skinned woman said, 'The path is wide.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave her alone, for she is insolent.'

key_terms.سَوْدَاءَ: A dark-skinned woman (often used as a descriptor or name)
key_terms.لَجَبَارَةٌ: Insolent, strong-willed, or possessing a dominant character

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'lajabarah' mean in the context of the dark-skinned woman's interaction with the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet (SAW) encounters a dark-skinned woman collecting dung who confidently asserts her right to the path, prompting him to describe her as 'lajabarah' (insolent or strong-willed). Shia scholars often interpret this not merely as a critique of arrogance, but as a nuanced observation of her dignified self-assurance despite her humble occupation, illustrating that true humility is a state of the heart rather than just social status. This incident serves as a practical lesson in recognizing the multifaceted nature of human character and the Prophet's acute perceptiveness in social dynamics.
